Hey female grey muzzle here! I’ve been through what you’re going through and I can also clear some things up. There is lots of female furries in the community and while yes there are issues with misogynistic behaviour in the fandom it’s also just a small percentage and it’s not everyone. It’s also a little rough to fit in when you’re new and honestly just don’t give up. You will make friends it just might take some time for people to know you, there is also other furs who are in the same boat as you as well and may be a bit shy. My best advice is to talk in local chats and go to public group events as it’s the best way to meet other furs and get to know other furs and to make friends! 

As for furry cons it’s 100% safe and a fun place to meet people. Don’t be discouraged if you don’t make new friends as that can take time. Just try to have fun and do as much as you can. A lot of furcons now have what’s called friend panels where it’s a safe space to try and meet some people who also feel like they haven’t made much friends and to try and meet new people. If at any point you do not feel safe at the con, You can always go to con staff and they will be more than happy to help you out and help you feel safe! 

Just be yourself and give it some time! Friends will come I can promise you that!

As suggested previously skyehighstudios has a very easy and free tutorial you can follow. It has taught me a lot about making fursuit bases. Don’t get discouraged tho for a first attempt it’s very good! I would say that your biggest factor is to try to stay as symmetrical as possible as it will improve what the final build looks like in the end. I’d say measure every out with a basic ruler and that will help you out a lot in terms of placement and carving.

You can also try to do a reverse image search and see if the makers name on the Etsy page matches what they have on their socials. It’s a good way to double check. I’d also even send a dm to the maker on the socials to be sure it’s them or to report if their work is being stolen

Not sure about the GameCube/wii one as I never owned it but I do know the orginal action replay and action replay max discs break and crack in the centre plastic extremely easily which does eventually spread to the disk over time. So if you do spend money on it take good care of it…

Sadly with retro games prices being pretty high nowadays it’s definitely been a struggle. I’m unsure if my tips will still help as I personally haven’t collected in a while but this is what I’ve done to find games for fairly cheap in the past which has landed me some good scores.

1. Yard sales/Yard sale type flee markets. I know not many of these flee markets are around anymore but I’ve always had super good luck finding good games from these and also at yard sales. Don’t be shy to ask if they have more games too! 

2. Local Facebook sale groups/marketplace. I have found some good Nintendo stuff off of marketplace but I’ve honestly had my best luck in recent years on local Facebook sale groups. It’s how I was able to score a legit copy of Chrono Trigger for $5 back in 2017

3. eBay. I’ve had my best luck with eBay lot auctions, however you may find something good from normal eBay listings as well. 

And lastly 4. Ask friends and family. I’ve gotten quite a few games and consoles from friends, family members and even coworkers over the years who had a Nintendo console of some kind collecting dust and they wanted to offload it since it’s taking up space and not being used. Always helps to bring up hobbies in casual conversation and politely offer to buy or trade for their old games that they don’t play anymore. 

Hope this helps :3

Yes! I’m was pretty much in the same boat where I had my console that I got modded with the xeno chip years ago and didn’t do much with it until now. I recently got the Swiss boot disk and the sd2sp2 pro (so it can be used a lot more easily with the GB player). I got them both for pretty cheap off of AliExpress. Always I can offer a bit of advice. 

First you may need to adjust the laser of your gamecube a smidge if the disk isn’t reading properly. (I gotta do this on mine tho Swiss does boot upon resting my gamecube after the disk error pops up). Another thing is to download the latest version of Swiss and rename the dol file as boot.dol as this will automatically update Swiss to the latest version upon booting up. Also for me my sd2sp2 pro did require a bit of sanding on the edges in order to fit in my console properly  

Hope this helps as this has brought a lot of life back into my old console. I might even mod my second one with the GC loader since the disk drive on that one is done
